q1_issues.issue: The for-phrase object is the NP "his first sporting passion", but the parse collapses it to the bare constant australian_football, dropping the passion witness, its possessive ("his"), the ordinal "first", and the apposition between the passion and Australian football.
The Name string "Lleyton Hewitt" does not preserve the surface form, which is "LLEYTON Hewitt".

q2_gaps: A proper noun used as a modifier inside a common-noun compound ("his Wimbledon title defence"): the compound rule absorbs "Wimbledon" into wimbledon_title_defence, while the naming rule requires every proper noun to keep its own symbol plus exactly one Name fact; nothing says which applies.

Temporal "as" as a simultaneity subordinator ("as the world champion relaxed"): the temporal-connective list names after/before/when/while/until/as-soon-as, and only during/while/throughout are mapped to During; bare "as" is never addressed.

An identity apposition between two co-referring descriptions set off by dashes ("his first sporting passion - Australian football -"): the appositive rule only covers typing an entity with a kind, not equating two descriptions.
notes: Roles, tense, the trade/relax During and relax/defence Before orderings, and the For-vs-Beneficiary split are all handled correctly; the loss is confined to the un-parsed "first sporting passion" NP.
